# Control Narrative: Fire Water Pump System (Module FW)

**Document:** CN-FW-001, Rev A (draft for review)
**Scope:** Site PLC/SCADA monitoring of fire pumps FP-1 and FP-2, jockey pump JP-1, and the fire water header.
**Governing codes:** NFPA 20 (pumps and controllers), NFPA 25 (inspection, testing, maintenance), NFPA 72 (supervisory signals). Confirm the adopted editions with the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ). See open item OI-01.

---

## 0. Corrections to the client's draft intent

The draft treats the fire pumps like process pumps. NFPA 20 assigns start, stop, and engine protection to the **listed fire pump controllers**. The site PLC must not hold any of these functions.

| # | Client draft intent | Correction | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-1 | PLC starts fire pumps on low header pressure | Each listed controller starts its own pump from its own pressure sensing line. The PLC only monitors and verifies that each pump starts when it should. | NFPA 20, electric and diesel controller chapters (automatic controllers, sensing lines) |
| C-2 | PLC stops pumps after pressure recovers for 10 min | Stop is **manual at the controller** by default. Automatic shutdown is a controller function. Use it only if the AHJ approves it. If it is used, the minimum run timer must be at least SP-06 (electric) and SP-07 (diesel). The client's single 10-min value is below the diesel minimum. The PLC never stops a fire pump. | NFPA 20 controller automatic-shutdown and minimum-run-timer provisions |
| C-3 | PLC trips FP-1 on low lube oil pressure and high coolant temperature | **Not permitted.** These conditions give alarms only. The engine runs to destruction during a fire, because losing the engine costs less than losing the fire water. Overspeed is the only automatic engine shutdown, and the engine's own overspeed device does it, not the PLC. | NFPA 20, diesel engine chapter (engine alarms and shutdowns) |
| C-4 | Pressure setpoints configured in the PLC | The setpoint spacing is acceptable (see SP-01 to SP-04). The values are set in the JP-1, FP-2, and FP-1 controllers, not in the PLC. Confirm JP-1 stop against fire pump churn plus maximum static suction pressure. Confirm that churn plus suction stays below the component pressure rating, or that a relief valve is provided. | NFPA 20 Annex (pressure maintenance setpoint guidance), NFPA 20 relief valve requirements |
| C-5 | PLC monitoring of run and trouble is the supervision | PLC monitoring is **supplementary**. Supervisory signals must also go to the fire alarm system at a constantly attended location. The PLC does not replace that path. | NFPA 20 controller signal requirements, NFPA 72 |
| C-6 | (implicit) PLC wired into controller circuits | Connect the PLC only through isolated dry contacts and a separate transmitter. No PLC fault, power loss, or cyber event can then change pump operation. The PLC has **no outputs** to FP-1, FP-2, or JP-1. | NFPA 20 controller listing integrity |

---

## Setpoint list (single source of truth)

Values marked "confirm" are provisional. Values in rows SP-01 to SP-09 live in the field controllers. The PLC does not use them for control. It holds copies only for display and for the expected-start checks.

| ID | Description | Value | Units | Where set | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | JP-1 stop pressure | 165 | psig | JP-1 controller | Given. Confirm ≥ FP churn + max static suction (OI-03) |
| SP-02 | JP-1 start pressure | 155 | psig | JP-1 controller | Given |
| SP-03 | FP-2 (electric, lead) start pressure | 145 | psig | FP-2 controller | Given |
| SP-04 | FP-1 (diesel, lag) start pressure | 135 | psig | FP-1 controller | Given |
| SP-05 | FP-1 / FP-2 automatic stop | Disabled (manual stop) | — | FP-1/FP-2 controllers | Confirm with AHJ (OI-02) |
| SP-06 | FP-2 minimum run timer, if auto-stop is approved | ≥ 10 | min | FP-2 controller | NFPA 20 minimum. Confirm edition |
| SP-07 | FP-1 minimum run timer, if auto-stop is approved | ≥ 30 | min | FP-1 controller | NFPA 20 minimum. Confirm edition |
| SP-08 | FP-1 crank cycle | 6 attempts × 15 s crank / 15 s rest | — | FP-1 controller | Listed controller standard. Confirm |
| SP-09 | FP-1 sequential start delay | 10 | s | FP-1 controller | Confirm (OI-04) |
| SP-10 | PLC check margin below controller start point (allows for PT-601 vs sensing-line location) | 5 | psi | PLC | Confirm at SAT |
| SP-11 | FP-2 expected-run delay | 30 | s | PLC | Confirm (includes ATS transfer) |
| SP-12 | FP-1 expected-run delay | 200 | s | PLC | Confirm (SP-08 full crank sequence + SP-09 + margin) |
| SP-13 | JP-1 expected-run delay | 15 | s | PLC | Confirm |
| SP-14 | JP-1 excessive starts | > 6 starts in 60 min | — | PLC | Confirm |
| SP-15 | JP-1 extended run | 30 | min | PLC | Confirm |
| SP-16 | Header high pressure (PT-601), no fire pump running | TBD | psig | PLC | Need component rating (OI-03) |
| SP-17 | LT-610 fuel refill warning | 75 | % of tank capacity | PLC | Provisional. Confirm |
| SP-18 | LT-610 low fuel (NFPA 25 minimum) | 66.7 (two-thirds) | % of tank capacity | PLC | Confirm edition |
| SP-19 | LT-610 high level (fill overflow) | 95 | % of tank capacity | PLC | Confirm (tank expansion volume) |
| SP-20 | Pump room low temperature (TT-611) | 70 | °F | PLC | Confirm vs engine maker minimum; see OI-05 |
| SP-21 | Pump room high temperature (TT-611) | 120 | °F | PLC | Confirm vs engine maker max air intake temperature |
| SP-22 | Analog bad-PV limits (PT-601, LT-610, TT-611) | < 3.6 or > 21.0 | mA | PLC | NAMUR NE 43. Confirm |
| SP-23 | Discrete alarm debounce | 2 | s | PLC | Confirm |
| SP-24 | FP-1 maximum interval between runs | 7 | days | PLC | NFPA 25 weekly. Confirm edition |
| SP-25 | FP-2 maximum interval between runs | 7 | days | PLC | NFPA 25 allows longer for some electric pumps. Confirm |
| SP-26 | Pressure restored prompt delay (pump running, PT-601 ≥ SP-02) | 5 | min | PLC | Confirm |

---

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

The fire water pumps supply the terminal fire water header. The listed controllers do all pump control. The site PLC monitors the system, verifies the expected responses, reports alarms, and keeps records.

- **Upstream:** fire water source and suction piping (by others, OI-06).
- **Downstream:** fire water header, hydrants, monitors, deluge and foam systems.
- **Interfaces:** fire alarm control panel (FACP) for code supervisory signals. Site SCADA for operator display and history.
- **Excluded from PLC scope:** pump start, pump stop, engine protection, ATS control, and jockey pump control.

## 2. Equipment and tags

No instrument index was given. The PLC module uses the tags below. Signal tags with suffixes are provisional until the instrument index is issued (OI-07).

| Tag | Description | Signal to PLC | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP-1 | Diesel fire pump, 2500 gpm at 150 psi, listed diesel controller | — | Given |
| FP-2 | Electric fire pump, 2500 gpm at 150 psi, listed electric controller with ATS | — | Given |
| JP-1 | Jockey pump, own controller | — | Given |
| PT-601 | Header pressure transmitter (monitor only) | AI, 4–20 mA | Given |
| LT-610 | FP-1 fuel tank level | AI, 4–20 mA | Given |
| TT-611 | Pump room temperature | AI, 4–20 mA | Tag provisional |
| FP-1.RUN / FP-2.RUN | Pump running | DI | Given |
| FP-1.FTS | FP-1 fail to start (overcrank) | DI | Given |
| FP-2.FTS | FP-2 fail to start | DI | Given |
| FP-1.TRBL / FP-2.TRBL | Controller common trouble | DI | Given |
| FP-1.AUTO / FP-2.AUTO | Controller not in automatic | DI | Proposed (OI-08) |
| FP-1.LOP / FP-1.HCT / FP-1.OVS | Low oil pressure / high coolant temp / overspeed shutdown | DI | Proposed (OI-08) |
| FP-1.BATT | Battery or charger failure | DI | Proposed (OI-08) |
| FP-2.PWR / FP-2.PHR / FP-2.ALT | Power or phase loss / phase reversal / ATS on alternate source | DI | Proposed (OI-08) |
| JP-1.RUN | Jockey pump running | DI | Proposed (OI-08) |

All trouble contacts are closed in the normal condition and open on alarm. A broken wire therefore gives an alarm.

## 3. States and transitions (ISA-106)

The PLC has **no transition authority**. The table defines the system states that the PLC infers from its inputs. The automation level of the system is automatic, by the listed controllers. The automation level of the PLC is monitor only.

| State | Definition (PLC inference) | Entry permissive | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|---|
| S0 Standby | All pumps stopped. PT-601 ≥ SP-02. | None | S1, S2, S3, S4 |
| S1 Pressure maintenance | JP-1 running. No fire pump running. | None | S0, S2 |
| S2 Demand – lead | FP-2 running. FP-1 stopped. | None | S3, S0 |
| S3 Demand – lead + lag | FP-1 running, with or without FP-2 | None | S2, S0 |
| S4 Test run | Fire pump running. Operator has set the HMI test flag. | Operator sets test flag | S0, S2, S3 |
| Overlay: Impaired | Any fire pump not available (Section 7, priority 1 or 2 availability alarms) | — | Clears when all causes clear |

| From | To | Condition | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | S1 | Pressure at JP-1 switch < SP-02 | JP-1 controller | Automatic |
| S1 | S0 | Pressure ≥ SP-01 and JP-1 minimum run complete | JP-1 controller | Automatic |
| S0/S1 | S2 | Pressure at FP-2 sensing line < SP-03 | FP-2 controller | Automatic |
| S0/S1 | S2 | Remote or local manual start | Operator at controller | Manual |
| S2 | S3 | Pressure at FP-1 sensing line < SP-04, after SP-09 | FP-1 controller | Automatic |
| S2/S3 | S0 | Operator pushes STOP at the controller after release by the incident commander | Operator at controller | Manual |
| S2/S3 | S0 | Controller auto-stop after SP-06/SP-07 (**only if SP-05 is enabled by AHJ approval**) | Controller | Automatic |
| S0 | S4 | Controller weekly test timer or manual test start, and operator sets test flag | Controller / operator | Operator-prompted |
| S4 | S0 | Pump stopped at controller, operator clears test flag | Operator | Manual |

Operations must sign off the states and prompts (OI-09).

## 4. Regulatory control

The PLC has no regulatory control loops in this module. Pressure maintenance is on/off control by JP-1 and the fire pump controllers. Tuning does not apply.

## 5. Sequences

The PLC has no control sequences. The tables below are **verification sequences**. The PLC compares the expected response of the listed controllers with what actually happens.

**Sequence V-1: Demand start verification**

| Step | Action (by field controller) | PLC transition condition | Timeout | PLC failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | JP-1 starts on low pressure | PT-601 < SP-02 − SP-10, then JP-1.RUN on | SP-13 | Alarm A-14 "JP-1 no run on demand" |
| 2 | FP-2 starts on low pressure | PT-601 < SP-03 − SP-10, then FP-2.RUN on | SP-11 | Alarm A-03 "FP-2 no run on demand" |
| 3 | FP-1 starts on low pressure | PT-601 < SP-04 − SP-10, then FP-1.RUN on | SP-12 | Alarm A-04 "FP-1 no run on demand" |
| 4 | Pumps continue to run | PT-601 ≥ SP-02 with a fire pump running | SP-26 | Prompt P-02 "Pressure restored". No stop command. |
| 5 | Operator stops pump at controller | FP-x.RUN off | None (operator action) | If FP-x.RUN goes off while PT-601 < SP-03, raise alarm A-05 |

**Sequence V-2: Test run record**

| Step | Action | PLC transition condition | Timeout | PLC failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Controller weekly timer or operator starts pump | FP-x.RUN on, PT-601 ≥ SP-03 | — | Prompt P-03 "Set test flag" |
| 2 | Operator sets test flag | Flag set | — | None. The run is logged as an unexplained run. |
| 3 | Pump stops | FP-x.RUN off | — | Log run duration |
| 4 | Next test due | No FP-x run for the interval | SP-24 / SP-25 | Alarm A-16 "Test run overdue" |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

No cause-and-effect chart was given. The rows below define the chart. Rows CE-01 to CE-09 are **listed controller functions**. They are verified at the NFPA 20 field acceptance test, not configured in the PLC.

| ID | Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CE-01 | FP-2 sensing pressure < SP-03 | Start FP-2 | Latched run (SP-05 disabled) | Manual STOP at FP-2 controller |
| CE-02 | FP-1 sensing pressure < SP-04, after SP-09 | Start FP-1 | Latched run (SP-05 disabled) | Manual STOP at FP-1 controller |
| CE-03 | FP-1 fails to start in SP-08 | Stop cranking, give fail-to-start signal | Latched | Manual reset at FP-1 controller |
| CE-04 | FP-1 engine overspeed | Shut down engine | Latched | Manual reset at engine overspeed device and controller |
| CE-05 | FP-1 low oil pressure | **Alarm only. No shutdown.** | Auto-reset alarm | None |
| CE-06 | FP-1 high coolant temperature | **Alarm only. No shutdown.** | Auto-reset alarm | None |
| CE-07 | FP-2 normal power loss | ATS transfers to alternate source | Auto | ATS retransfer per ATS settings |
| CE-08 | JP-1 pressure < SP-02 | Start JP-1 | Auto-reset | Stops at SP-01 |
| CE-09 | JP-1 pressure ≥ SP-01 | Stop JP-1 | Auto-reset | — |
| CE-10 | Any PLC condition, fault, or power loss | **No effect on FP-1, FP-2, JP-1, or ATS** | — | — |

**SIS:** The fire water system is not a safety instrumented system under IEC 61511. It has no SIF and no SRS. If the terminal HAZOP or LOPA credits fire water as a mitigation layer, the reference goes in that study (OI-10).

## 7. Alarms

No rationalized alarm database was given. The PLC needs the alarms below. Priorities are provisional until ISA-18.2 rationalization (OI-11). Code supervisory signals also go to the FACP (C-5).

| ID | Alarm | Source | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-01 | FP-1 running | FP-1.RUN | On, test flag not set | 1 | Find the fire or flow event. Send an operator to the pump house. |
| A-02 | FP-2 running | FP-2.RUN | On, test flag not set | 1 | Same as A-01 |
| A-03 | FP-2 no run on demand | V-1 step 2 | SP-11 elapsed | 1 | Send operator to FP-2 controller. Start FP-2 locally. Start impairment procedure. |
| A-04 | FP-1 no run on demand | V-1 step 3 | SP-12 elapsed | 1 | Same as A-03 for FP-1 |
| A-05 | Fire pump stopped at low pressure | FP-x.RUN off | PT-601 < SP-03 | 1 | Send operator to restart the pump |
| A-06 | FP-1 fail to start | FP-1.FTS | On | 1 | Reset at controller after cause found. Start impairment procedure. |
| A-07 | FP-2 fail to start | FP-2.FTS | On | 1 | Same as A-06 |
| A-08 | FP-1 / FP-2 controller trouble | FP-x.TRBL | On, SP-23 | 2 | Send operator to read the controller display |
| A-09 | FP-x not in automatic | FP-x.AUTO | On, SP-23 | 2 | Return controller to AUTO, or start impairment procedure |
| A-10 | FP-1 low oil pressure / high coolant temperature (running) | FP-1.LOP / HCT | On | 2 | Do not stop FP-1 during a fire. Send a mechanic. Tell the incident commander. |
| A-11 | FP-1 overspeed shutdown | FP-1.OVS | On | 1 | Reset at engine. Start impairment procedure. |
| A-12 | FP-1 battery or charger failure | FP-1.BATT | On | 2 | Send electrician |
| A-13 | FP-2 power loss, phase reversal, or on alternate source | FP-2.PWR / PHR / ALT | On | 2 | Tell electrical. Monitor ATS. |
| A-14 | JP-1 no run on demand | V-1 step 1 | SP-13 elapsed | 3 | Check JP-1 controller |
| A-15 | JP-1 excessive starts / extended run | JP-1.RUN | SP-14 / SP-15 | 3 | Look for header leakage |
| A-16 | Fire pump test run overdue | V-2 step 4 | SP-24 / SP-25 | 3 | Schedule test per NFPA 25 |
| A-17 | Fuel refill required | LT-610 | < SP-17 | 3 | Order fuel |
| A-18 | Fuel below minimum | LT-610 | < SP-18 | 2 | Refill. Start impairment procedure if refill is late. |
| A-19 | Fuel tank high | LT-610 | > SP-19 | 2 | Stop the fuel delivery |
| A-20 | Pump room low / high temperature | TT-611 | < SP-20 / > SP-21 | 2 | Check heating or ventilation |
| A-21 | Header high pressure | PT-601 | > SP-16, no FP running | 2 | Check JP-1 stop and relief valve |
| A-22 | Demand exceeds pump capacity | PT-601 | < SP-04 − SP-10 with both FP running, SP-27 | 1 | Tell the incident commander. Reduce open fire water users. |
| A-23 | Analog signal bad | PT-601 / LT-610 / TT-611 | Outside SP-22 | 3 | Send instrument technician |

## 8. Abnormal handling

| Condition | PLC behavior | Effect on pumps |
|---|---|---|
| PT-601 bad PV | Raise A-23. Freeze the display value with a bad-quality flag. Disable V-1 timing checks. Keep all discrete alarms active. | None. Controllers use their own sensing lines. |
| LT-610 or TT-611 bad PV | Raise A-23. Disable the related level or temperature alarms. | None |
| Discrete input wire break | Contact opens, so the related trouble alarm comes on | None |
| PLC-to-SCADA comms loss | Raise comms alarm at SCADA. PLC keeps logging locally. | None. FACP stays the supervisory path. |
| PLC power loss | All PLC alarms are lost. SCADA raises a comms alarm. | None |
| PLC restart | Read all inputs. Re-establish state from inputs. Do not raise A-03/A-04 for runs that started before the restart. Issue no commands (the PLC has no outputs). | None |
| Site normal power loss | FP-2 ATS transfers (CE-07). FP-1 runs on its batteries. | Pumps stay available |
| Fail positions | The PLC has no outputs to the pump system, so no PLC fail position applies. Field controllers fail to "available for automatic start". | — |

## 9. Operator interface

The operator sees:

- PT-601 value and trend, with SP-01 to SP-04 shown as reference lines.
- Run, auto, and trouble status for FP-1, FP-2, and JP-1.
- LT-610 in percent, and TT-611.
- Impairment banner, run log, and test-due dates.

The operator can change only the test flag and alarm acknowledgment. The HMI has **no start or stop commands** for FP-1, FP-2, or JP-1.

**WARNING:** Do not stop FP-1 or FP-2 until the incident commander releases the fire water system. A stopped pump can cause loss of fire water pressure.

| Prompt | Trigger | Text |
|---|---|---|
| P-01 | A-01 or A-02 | "Fire pump running. Find the cause. Send an operator to the pump house." |
| P-02 | V-1 step 4 | "Header pressure restored. Get release from the incident commander. Stop the pump at the controller." |
| P-03 | V-2 step 1 | "Fire pump running at normal pressure. Set the test flag if this is a test." |

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-FW-001 | The PLC shall have no outputs to FP-1, FP-2, JP-1, or the ATS. | Drawing review; FAT I/O check |
| FR-FW-002 | Each fire pump shall start from its listed controller on its own sensing line (CE-01, CE-02). | NFPA 20 field acceptance test, witnessed |
| FR-FW-003 | Fire pumps shall stop only by manual STOP at the controller, unless SP-05 is enabled. | Field acceptance test |
| FR-FW-004 | FP-1 shall not shut down on low oil pressure or high coolant temperature. | Field acceptance test (simulated signal) |
| FR-FW-005 | FP-1 shall shut down on overspeed and latch until manual reset. | Field acceptance test |
| FR-FW-006 | The PLC shall raise A-03 and A-04 per V-1. | FAT (simulated PT-601 and RUN inputs) |
| FR-FW-007 | The PLC shall raise every alarm in Section 7 at its listed condition. | FAT, then SAT |
| FR-FW-008 | All trouble inputs shall alarm on open circuit. | SAT (lift a wire at each input) |
| FR-FW-009 | PLC power loss shall not change the state of any pump. | SAT (remove PLC power during a JP-1 run) |
| FR-FW-010 | After restart, the PLC shall rebuild state from inputs and raise no false A-03 or A-04. | FAT |
| FR-FW-011 | Bad PV on PT-601 shall disable V-1 timing checks and raise A-23. | FAT (inject out-of-range signal) |
| FR-FW-012 | The HMI shall show no fire pump start or stop command. | FAT graphic review |
| FR-FW-013 | The HMI shall show prompts P-01 to P-03 at their triggers. | FAT |
| FR-FW-014 | The PLC shall log each pump run with start time, duration, and test flag. | FAT |
| FR-FW-015 | The FACP shall receive the code supervisory signals independently of the PLC. | Fire alarm acceptance test, by others |

**Review notes:** The minimum run timers, crank cycle, fuel minimum, and room temperatures above are typical NFPA 20/25 values. Verify them against the edition the AHJ enforces before the setpoint list leaves "confirm" status. After construction starts, change this document only through MOC.
